source.version: IZA Discussion Paper No. 17302, dated September 2024 (working paper). Locators below give the PDF page first; the printed page number equals the PDF page minus 2.
source.title_on_document: Creative and Strategic Capabilities of Generative AI: Evidence from Large-Scale Experiments

supplement.where: The paper says: "Comprehensive experimental instructions and additional data supporting our conclusions are available in the supplementary materials." (PDF p. 12, printed p. 10, end of Section 2.2). No URL given.
supplement.holds: Experimental instructions and unspecified additional data. The appendix in this PDF (Tables 13-16, Figures 6-8, PDF pp. 33-40) holds the sub-dimension regressions, the >180s robustness table, and the unique-idea curves; all statistics coded here are in this PDF.

paper_design_summary: 1,250 US adults on Prolific were randomly assigned to write one creative text (up to 1,000 characters, max 10 minutes) either alone (HumanBaseline, 688), alone but told they compete with AI (HumanAgainstAI, 253), or with access to Bard or ChatGPT 3.5/4 (HumanPlusAI, 309). ChatGPT-4 and Bard produced 224 and 216 texts for the same prompts. 3,336 separate Prolific raters, randomized to three information conditions, and five research assistants rated every text 0-10 on creativity, originality, surprise and usefulness; the paper also counts unique ideas per source with sBERT embeddings and hierarchical clustering, and runs a rock-paper-scissors strategic task.

studies.label: Writer experiment (creative text with or without AI access)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Writing condition: HumanBaseline (no AI, standard top-10% bonus), HumanAgainstAI (no AI, told entries compete with AI texts for the bonus), HumanPlusAI (may use Bard or ChatGPT 3.5/4 to produce the text).
assignment.quote: Human participants were randomly assigned to one of three treatments
assignment.prereg_locator: PDF p. 3, title footnote: "pre-registered on AEA Registry, AEARCTR-0011584"; PDF p. 9 footnote 3 gives preregistered targets of 700, 300 and 300 participants

arms.name: HumanBaseline
arms.description: Writes the creative text alone; top 10% most creative humans receive a GBP 5 bonus.

arms.name: HumanAgainstAI
arms.description: Writes alone but is told the entry competes with human and AI-generated texts for the top-10% bonus.

arms.name: HumanPlusAI
arms.description: Had the choice to use Bard or ChatGPT (3.5 or 4); declared the tool before writing (Bard 39, ChatGPT-3.5 184, ChatGPT-4 86). Prolific listing requested participants who already had an OpenAI or Bard account.

participants.exclusions: Section 2.1.1 lists 688, 253 and 309 participants (sum 1,250, matching the 1,250 recruited and the Table 1 N). Footnote 3 says the paper received 702, 304 and 315 complete responses against targets of 700, 300 and 300; the paper does not explain the gap between 1,321 complete responses and the 1,250 analyzed. No count is given at the moment of assignment, so n_randomized is null. Table 15 drops writers who spent under 180 seconds (19.5 percent of participants) as a robustness check.
participants.who: US adults recruited on Prolific; described as a representative population of US adults; mean age about 44, about 49 percent male (Table 1).
participants.quote: We recruited 1250 participants from the U.S. through the Prolific platform to participate in a divergent (unconstrained) creative task
participants.locator: PDF p. 9 (printed p. 7), Section 2.1.1; arm counts PDF pp. 9-10; Table 1 PDF p. 13 (printed p. 11)

ai_tool.name_model: Google Bard, ChatGPT-3.5 or ChatGPT-4 through participants' own accounts (Bard 39, ChatGPT-3.5 184, ChatGPT-4 86; footnote 4)
ai_tool.how_used: Participants in HumanPlusAI "had the choice to utilize Bard or ChatGPT (3.5 or 4) for help in producing their responses" and declared which tool they would use before writing; the introduction says they "were instructed to use them when generating the answers" (PDF p. 5). Use was not logged in the reported analysis.

task.description: Divergent creativity task after Charness and Grieco (2019): write a text of up to 1,000 characters (about 150 words), as creative as possible, on one of two prompts: "If you had the talent to invent things just by thinking of them, what would you create?" or "Imagine and describe a town, city, or society in the future." GBP 2 base pay; GBP 5 bonus for texts in the top 10 percent by rater scores.

outcomes.name: Overall creativity rated by online raters ("In general, how creative was this response?", 0-10)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Prolific raters (3,336 after exclusions, across three rater conditions) each rated 20 random texts; every text rated at least 10 times (a few 8 or 9). OLS on individual ratings with rater fixed effects; SEs clustered at the response (text) level; each writer produced one text. Reference group HumanBaseline; the regression pools ratings of ChatGPT-4 and Bard texts too. Robustness: prompt control (col 2), all controls (col 5), gender interactions (cols 6-8), writers >180 s only (Table 15).

contrasts.reported: Table 2: HumanPlusAI 0.500*** (0.052) in col (1) no controls and col (2) prompt control; 0.474*** (0.052) col (5) all controls (46,845 obs); by gender col (6): Female 0.565*** (0.065), Male 0.435*** (0.073). Observations 63,812. Table 15 (writing time >180 s): 0.458*** (0.054) col (1), 54,771 obs. Table 3 means for HumanPlusAI texts by tool: Bard 5.57 (n=39), ChatGPT 3.5 5.93 (n=184), ChatGPT 4.0 5.84 (n=86); no HumanBaseline mean printed.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 15 (printed p. 13), Table 2; PDF p. 16 (printed p. 14), Table 3; PDF p. 37 (printed p. 35), Table 15

outcomes.measure_detail: Five RAs (two art-school students in Lausanne, three business-school students) rated all texts in the CorrectedRaters condition (grammar-corrected human texts). OLS with rater and rating-order fixed effects; SEs clustered by response. The paper calls this a robustness check. Coded human_raters because the RAs are students, not domain professionals.

outcomes.name: Ratio of unique ideas within each condition's pool of texts
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Each text embedded with Sentence-BERT (all-mpnet-base-v2); pairwise cosine distances within each source; hierarchical clustering with Ward linkage; clusters below a global distance threshold count as one idea; ratio = unique ideas / number of texts. Reported at thresholds 0.5 and 1 for all texts, the top 100 texts within each source, and the top 10 percent of texts pooled across sources; Figures 6-8 show all thresholds. Table 7 labels the AI-access arm "HumanAndAI".

contrasts.reported: Point values only, no test or uncertainty. Table 7, ALL texts: HumanAndAI 29.9% vs HumanBaseline 30.2% (threshold 0.5); 7.3% vs 6.7% (threshold 1). Top 100 within source: 38.0% vs 52.0% (0.5); 6.0% vs 10.0% (1). Top 10% pooled: 50.0% vs 64.5% (0.5); 12.5% vs 9.7% (1). HumanAgainstAI ALL: 35.9% (0.5), 6.9% (1).
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 23 (printed p. 21), Table 7; method PDF pp. 21-22 (printed pp. 19-20), Section 3.1.4; Figures 6-8 PDF pp. 39-40

diversity_detail.metric: Ratio of unique ideas (number of clusters below a global distance threshold divided by number of texts); higher means more diverse
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairwise cosine distances among texts within each source/condition, then Ward hierarchical clustering of that condition's pool
diversity_detail.uncertainty: None reported; one ratio per condition and threshold
diversity_detail.notes: Sign: higher ratio = more diverse, so no reversal needed. Pools differ in size (309 HumanPlusAI vs 688 HumanBaseline texts in ALL; 100 each in Top 100), which may affect the ratio; the paper does not discuss this.

eligibility.reason: S1: the paper states that writers were randomly assigned to HumanPlusAI (AI chatbot access, 309) or HumanBaseline (no AI, 688) among three arms (PDF p. 9); 1,250 writers analyzed; creativity, originality, surprise and usefulness are rated by blind raters on the writers' texts, and a diversity measure is computed on them. Caveat for review: the Prolific description for the AI arm requested people who already had an OpenAI or Bard account, and footnote 3 gives per-arm recruitment targets, so it is not fully clear whether HumanPlusAI was recruited from the same pool at the moment of randomization. S2 (AI vs human texts) is context of type ai_vs_human.

one_line_finding: Writers randomly given access to Bard or ChatGPT scored 0.500 points higher (SE 0.052, 0-10 scale) on online-rater creativity than unassisted writers (Table 2, PDF p. 15) and 0.142 (SE 0.067) with five RAs (Table 5, PDF p. 19), but RAs rated them lower on originality (-0.416, SE 0.088; Table 16) and the unique-idea ratio was about equal (29.9% vs 30.2% at threshold 0.5; Table 7, PDF p. 23).
open_questions: Was HumanPlusAI recruited from the same Prolific pool as the other arms? The paper says writers were randomly assigned but also that the AI-arm listing requested participants with an OpenAI or Bard account (PDF p. 10) and gives per-arm targets (footnote 3, PDF p. 9).
Footnote 3 reports 702, 304 and 315 complete responses, but the analysis uses 688, 253 and 309; the paper does not say why 71 responses are missing.
No HumanBaseline arm mean or SD for creativity is printed; only regression coefficients on rating-level data with SEs clustered by response (one response per writer).
Text on PDF p. 18 says HumanPlusAI was not statistically more creative than HumanBaseline in RA ratings, while Table 5 shows 0.142** (0.067).
notes: PDF page = printed page + 2. Table 4 (PDF p. 18) also reports the share of top-10/5/1 percent texts by source (HumanPlusAI 31, 17, 3). A follow-up survey two months later collected only self-reports (income, self-rated creativity), not a new creative output, so there is no after_ai outcome. The candidate record's note that HumanPlusAI use was optional matches the text ("had the choice"), but footnote 4 assigns all 309 participants to a tool (Bard 39, ChatGPT-3.5 184, ChatGPT-4 86). Rater experiment (S3) and strategic task (S4) are listed for completeness; they have no outcomes on the three questions.
